ok, I need to say something because this is really upsetting me. A sticker shop called StickerBurrow Co is selling my switchblade moth as a vinyl decal. It’s listed as “Knife Moth Vinyl Decal” for $6.50, or 3 for $15.

I drew that moth for my Sept 13 flash day and posted the sheet on Aug 30. It went to a client in the first hour. Flash is sold one time to one person. That’s the deal, and that client paid for it. I did not sell the design to a sticker company, give anyone permission to print it, or make stickers of somebody’s tattoo.

And to the person who got the moth tattooed: I’m so sorry this has landed in your lap. I did not sell your tattoo or authorize these stickers. I can understand why seeing it for sale would make you wonder, and I wanted to say that clearly without putting your business out there.

I’ve seen the listing. It’s not “inspired by” my work. It’s a straight scan of my linework: same crack in the blade, same wing pattern, and they didn’t even flip it. I messaged them asking them to take it down and told them it was my design from my flash sheet. Their reply started with “love your work!” and then went to “moths are a very common tattoo motif,” and basically told me to send a registered copyright through their support form.

I know moths are a common motif. That is not the point. A common motif doesn’t explain the exact same little details, in the exact same arrangement, down to the crack in the blade. I drew this. Somebody else is selling it.

Small shops and independent artists don’t have lawyer money to throw at every company that decides to ignore us. These sticker places know that. It’s exhausting to be told to jump through hoops while someone else makes money off work you spent hours drawing.

If you want to help, please report the listing through the platform and don’t buy from them. Please don’t harass anyone or go after their other pages; just report the listing. And please don’t tag the shop page into this. This is my personal page, and I’m keeping it here.

I’m mad, honestly. But I also want other artists and clients to know: when you buy a flash piece, you’re buying the agreed tattoo, not signing up to have your design show up on somebody else’s merch.

reasons: The post never says the client messaged Jo that night thinking Jo was selling stickers of her tattoo; it only hints that she might 'wonder', so that required point is missing.
